title: Reimagining how product teams make decisions with AI
jpTitle: AI による UX ワークフローの変革
role: Lead Product Designer (Agentic UX & AI Systems)

summary.en: Inside a locked-down enterprise where Gemini and NotebookLM were the only AI allowed, I interviewed the team, mapped 40+ friction points, and built ten purpose-built agents into the workflow people already used. Rolled out from 42 designers to 80+ cross-functional stakeholders.
summary.jp: 閉じた企業環境で使える AI は Gemini と NotebookLM のみ。取材で 40 件超のつまずきを地図にした。既存業務に 10 体のエージェントを組み込み、42 人から 80 人超まで広がった。

product.en: The problem was never the tools; it was where decisions got made. Ten agents — a shared Master Brain, an edge-case detector, a CX strategist grounded in real heuristics — moved product, design and engineering decisions earlier, where fixing them costs a fraction of what it costs in development.
product.jp: 問題は道具ではなく、判断がどこで起きるかだった。共有の知識役、見落とし検知役、実際の評価基準に基づく助言役。10 体のエージェントが、製品・設計・開発の判断をより早い段階に動かした。

transformation.en: AI transformation without a decree: start with the team's actual pain, build agents where it hurts, share every one live in weekly workshops, and let a product-strategy team take ownership. 42 designers, then 80+ people across PM, research and content, six brands.
transformation.jp: 号令ではない広め方。まずチームの実際の困りごとから始めた。痛いところにエージェントを置き、毎週の勉強会で全部見せた。最後は現場のチームに引き渡した。

creative-tech.en: Working inside hard constraints — no custom models, no API access, Gemini and NotebookLM only — as a design brief. Agents authored as small filesystems of workflow, definition and knowledge files; Figma wired to code through MCP so prototypes stay on the real design system.
creative-tech.jp: 独自モデルも API 接続もない制約を、設計条件にした。エージェントは手順・定義・知識の小さなファイル群として書いた。Figma は MCP でコードとつなぎ、試作が設計基盤から外れないようにした。

mine: 16 one-hour deep-dive interviews with designers and strategists in late 2025, about the working day rather than the deliverables; transcripts clustered with NotebookLM into a searchable pain map

Categorised the transcripts into 40+ distinct friction points and scored each on severity, business impact, ease of change and AI opportunity; selected the bets with design leadership off the resulting heat map

Designed and built all ten agents: Master Brain (3-layer project knowledge hub), Justin Case (edge-case detector), Sally (CX strategist / heuristic evaluator), the five-agent WDS studio, Clara (UX-writing evaluator), Alex (agent architect)
Authored agents as filesystems of workflow, definition and knowledge files; iterated each 'Gem' version after version
Wired Figma to VS Code via MCP so AI prototypes run on real design-system code
Weekly hands-on workshops for ~40 designers; every agent shared live
team: The XM product-strategy team took ownership of Master Brain and ran it across multiple real projects
Design leadership selected which bets to pilot
Designers, PMs, researchers and content people adopted the agents in their own projects

narrative.situation: Gemini became the only AI allowed inside Verizon's enterprise stack, and nobody knew what to do with it.
narrative.problem: Business and Technology scoped every project before design entered the room; with no budget to test, the highest-position opinion won; by handoff, good UX was already out of scope. Project knowledge was fragmented across people and documents.
failureModes: Tribal knowledge trap — business logic, requirements and institutional knowledge fragmented across email and people rather than a repository, producing rework and losing product intelligence when staff left
Late-phase discovery — technical discovery and SME collaboration arrived after handoff, so edge cases surfaced as emergency rework
Designing in the dark — no dedicated budget or timeline for user testing, so stakeholder opinion stood in for validated data and no decision could be justified objectively
Strategic design compression — delivery pressure pushed designers into pixel pushing, spending the time that strategic rigour needed
narrative.opportunity: Put AI at the exact moments where the process hurt — inside the workflow everyone already used — rather than rewriting the org.
constraints: Gemini and NotebookLM only. No custom models, no API access.
built: Four steps inserted ahead of handoff, where the old workflow had only sequential handoffs and late validation: an initiative alignment document, edge-case detection, a functional prototype, and synthetic usability testing

Master Brain — centralized project knowledge (brand, research, project layers), assembled from project documentation, recorded meeting transcripts, strategic direction from design leadership, and outside market and competitor intelligence; reusable brand and research brains compose into the project one
Justin Case — lightweight validation agent for early edge-case detection
Sally — AI-assisted heuristic and CX evaluation
Alex — meta-agent that designs new agents

organizational: Designers shifted from tactical execution to strategic decision support
Fragmented knowledge consolidated into one source of truth
Rollout expanded from 42 designers to 80+ cross-functional stakeholders across six brands
business: Late-stage UX and engineering rework reduced by catching edge cases at ideation

_notes: The case-study page carries a confidentiality notice: specific metrics, tooling and instructions are generalized. Metrics here are the ones the page states.
Engagement type is not stated on the page; left as 'unstated' rather than guessed.
The 10× rework figure is an industry rule of thumb quoted on the page, so it is 'unverified' and no Lens can highlight it.

The workflow, the four failure modes and the Master Brain inputs are taken from the AI Powered Workflow Training Workshop deck (docs/verizon-work-transformation-slides.md). That deck states no measured time-saved, adoption, quality or revenue KPI, so none has been added here — its outcome claims are qualitative.

name.jp: Verizon AI ワークフロー

oneLiner.en: Ten agents built into the tools 42 designers already used.
oneLiner.jp: 42 人のデザイナーがすでに使っている道具の中に、10 体のエージェントを入れた。

challenge.en: Business and Technology scoped every project before design entered the room. With no budget to test, the highest-position opinion won, and by handoff good UX was already out of scope. Project knowledge sat scattered across people, emails and research PDFs nobody had time to read. Gemini and NotebookLM were the only AI allowed.
challenge.jp: デザインが呼ばれる前に、ビジネスと技術がプロジェクトの範囲を決めていた。検証の予算はなく、いちばん役職の高い人の意見が通る。引き渡しの頃には、良い UX はもう範囲の外だった。知識は人とメールと、誰も読む暇のない調査 PDF に散らばっていた。使える AI は Gemini と NotebookLM だけ。

solution.en: I didn't try to rewrite the org. I put AI at the exact moments the process hurt, inside the workflow people already used: interviews with 16 designers, 40+ friction points, ten single-purpose agents. The decisive move was building each agent as a small filesystem — workflow, definition, knowledge — so it stayed reliable as use spread from 42 designers to 80+ stakeholders across six brands.
solution.jp: 組織を書き換えようとはしなかった。みんながすでに使っている業務の、痛いところにだけ AI を置いた。デザイナー 16 人に話を聞き、40 件超のつまずきを洗い出し、役目をひとつに絞ったエージェントを 10 体つくった。決め手は、各エージェントを「手順・定義・知識」の小さなファイル群として組んだこと。42 人から 6 ブランド 80 人超へ広がっても、動きがぶれなかった。
